title: Numeric types: signed and unsigned integers, floats and complex numbers

videos.script: Lesson 6 gave every variable a zero value. This lesson is about what the numbers themselves can hold. An integer in Go has a fixed size, and the size is a limit. {{limits}} The program on screen adds one to the largest eight-bit integer. It does not fail. It wraps around to minus one hundred and twenty-eight. {{wrap}} Division drops the fraction, and dividing by zero stops the program with a panic. {{floats}} Then floating point. Add point one and point two in two variables, and the answer is not point three. You will see the sixty-four bits that explain why. {{nan}} Floats also have infinity, and a value called NaN that is not even equal to itself. {{money}} That is why money in this course is counted in whole cents, never in floats. {{complex}} Last, complex numbers, which Go has built in. By the end you can choose a numeric type, and say what happens at the edge of each one.
